title: Noetherian flat geometrically integral algebra is projective
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian commutative ring and let $R\to S$ be a finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] flat homomorphism of commutative rings. Assume that every fibre ring $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is geometrically integral over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ for every $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}(R)$. Then $S$ is a projective $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] [def-weil-residue-field] [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible].

proof.text: We first record explicitly the base-change calculations used below. For any $R$-algebra $T$, put $S_T=S\otimes_RT$. Images $s_i\otimes1$ of finite algebra generators $s_i$ of $S$ generate $S_T$ over $T$: expand each $s$ as a polynomial in the $s_i$ and balance its coefficients in each pure tensor. If $U\hookrightarrow V$ is an injection of $T$-modules, the maps $U\otimes_T(S\otimes_RT)\simeq U\otimes_RS$, $u\otimes(s\otimes t)\mapsto tu\otimes s$, with inverse $u\otimes s\mapsto u\otimes(s\otimes1)$, and the same maps for $V$, identify its tensor with $S_T$ with tensoring the original injection over $R$ with $S$. Thus $S_T$ is $T$-flat by [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. These inverse formulas are well defined by the bilinearity relations [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.place: Tag 05FS, lemma-fibres-irreducible-flat-projective, proof, finite type and flatness under base change, expanded

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak p'\subset T$ contract to $\mathfrak p\subset R$. The induced map $R/\mathfrak p\hookrightarrow\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ extends to a field embedding $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\hookrightarrow\kappa(\mathfrak p')$, since every nonzero denominator stays nonzero. Tensor balancing [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives $S_T\otimes_T\kappa(\mathfrak p')\simeq(S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\kappa(\mathfrak p')$, sending $(s\otimes t)\otimes\lambda$ to $(s\otimes1)\otimes\bar t\lambda$ and inversely $(s\otimes a)\otimes\lambda\mapsto(s\otimes1)\otimes\bar a\lambda$. The same formulas hold after every further field extension of $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$. Hence all fibres of $T\to S_T$ are geometrically integral because every field extension of each original fibre $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is a nonzero domain by hypothesis. In particular the hypotheses persist for $T=R/I$ and for the completion used later.

source.place: Tag 05FS, lemma-fibres-irreducible-flat-projective, proof, geometric integrality under base change, expanded

proof.text: Assume the set of ideals $I\subseteq R$ for which $S/IS$ is not projective over $R/I$ is nonempty. The ascending chain condition gives a maximal member $I$. It is proper, since $S/RS=0$ is projective over the zero ring. Put $J=\sqrt I$. The ideal $J/I$ is finitely generated and every generator is nilpotent; if their nilpotence exponents are $e_1,\ldots,e_r$, every monomial of degree $1+\sum(e_i-1)$ vanishes, so $J/I$ is nilpotent. If $I\ne J$, maximality gives projectivity of $S/JS$, while Step 1 gives flatness of $S/IS$ over $R/I$. Applying [lem-trf-local-nilpotent-projective-flat-lift] contradicts the choice of $I$. Thus $I$ is radical. Replace $(R,S)$ by $(R/I,S/IS)$, retaining the hypotheses by Steps 1--2. The quotient is Noetherian because generators of the inverse image of an ideal descend to generators. We now have a nonzero reduced Noetherian ring $R$, with $S$ not projective but $S/JS$ projective over $R/J$ for every nonzero ideal $J$.

proof.text: Let $A=R^\wedge=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}R/(f^n)$ and $N=S\otimes_RA$. By [lem-trf-local-completion-product-faithfully-flat], $R\to R_f\times A$ is faithfully flat. The completion $A$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian]. Since $(f)$ is generated by one element, [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] gives that $A$ is $fA$-adically complete and gives the canonical $R$-algebra isomorphism $A/fA\simeq R/(f)$. We will verify the hypotheses of [lem-trf-local-flat-pure-complete-projective] with base $A$, algebra $B=N$, module $M=N$ and ideal $fA$.

source.place: Tag 05FS, lemma-fibres-irreducible-flat-projective, proof, completion and the criterion of Tag 05DP

proof.text: Step 1 gives that $A\to N$ is finite type and flat; $N$ is a finite $N$-module, generated by $1$. The isomorphism of Step 5 gives $N/fN\simeq S/fS$: explicitly $(s\otimes a)\bmod fN\mapsto s\bar a\bmod fS$, where $\bar a\in R/(f)$ is the projection of $a$, and $s\bmod fS\mapsto(s\otimes1)\bmod fN$ is its inverse. These are well defined and inverse by the tensor relations [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and $A/fA\simeq R/(f)$. They are linear over the identified base rings. Since $(f)\ne0$, the maximal-bad-ideal reduction in Step 3 makes $S/fS$ projective over $R/(f)$, hence $N/fN$ projective over $A/fA$.

source.place: Tag 05FS, lemma-fibres-irreducible-flat-projective, proof, projective reduction and base-change hypotheses, expanded

proof.text: Fix a prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$ and put $F=N\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. By Step 2, $F$ is a nonzero domain. Consider $D=N/\mathfrak pN$ and $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p)=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Step 1 applied again to $A\to N$ shows that $D$ is flat over $A/\mathfrak p$. Tensoring the injection $A/\mathfrak p\hookrightarrow K$ with $D$ injects $D\hookrightarrow D\otimes_{A/\mathfrak p}K=F$, by [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. This injection sends $1$ to $1$, so $D$ is a nonzero domain and $A/\mathfrak p\to D$ is injective (compose it with the field embedding into $F$). Therefore $\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p}=\mathfrak pN$ is prime, contracts to $\mathfrak p$, and is exactly the kernel of $N\to F$. For every $0\ne z\in F$, $bz=0$ if and only if the image of $b\in N$ in $F$ is zero. Thus $\operatorname{Ann}_N(z)=\mathfrak pN$. Since $z=1$ is allowed, the associated primes of $F$ as an $N$-module are exactly $\{\mathfrak pN\}$, by [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes]. No assertion is made about all primes of $N$ lying over $\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Tag 05FS, lemma-fibres-irreducible-flat-projective, proof, identification of the sole associated prime of each fibre, expanded

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-complete-jacobson-radical] for the complete pair $(A,fA)$, every maximal ideal of $A$ contains $f$. Choose a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ containing $\mathfrak p$; then $\mathfrak p+fA\subseteq\mathfrak m$. Step 7 applied to $\mathfrak m$ supplies the proper prime $\mathfrak mN$ of $N$. It contains $fN+\mathfrak pN$, so $fN+\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p}\ne N$. This is precisely the associated-prime condition of [lem-trf-local-flat-pure-complete-projective], for every associated prime identified in Step 7. The use of a prime over $\mathfrak m$ is essential: membership of $f$ in the Jacobson radical of $A$ alone does not imply membership in the Jacobson radical of $N$.

source.place: Tag 05FS, lemma-fibres-irreducible-flat-projective, proof, properness of fN plus the associated prime, expanded

proof.text: All hypotheses of [lem-trf-local-flat-pure-complete-projective] now hold for $(A,fA,N,N)$: Noetherianity and completeness are Step 5, finite type, finiteness, flatness and projective reduction are Step 6, and the condition on every associated prime of every fibre is Steps 7--8. It follows that $N$ is projective as an $A$-module.

source.place: Tag 05FS, lemma-fibres-irreducible-flat-projective, proof, application of Tag 05DP

proof.text: Write $C=R_f\times A$. The two central idempotents split $S\otimes_RC\simeq S_f\times N$, as a $C$-module. Freeness makes $S_f$ projective, and Step 9 makes $N$ projective. This pair is projective over $C$: a surjection and a map from it decompose by the same two idempotents, and componentwise projectivity supplies lifts whose pair is a $C$-linear lift. Apply [lem-trf-local-projective-faithfully-flat-descent] to the faithfully flat map $R\to C$ of Step 5. It follows that $S$ is projective over $R$, contradicting Step 3. The set of bad ideals was therefore empty, and the original $S$ is projective over the original $R$.
